The woman WHO wears a red shirt: ที่.
A palavra interrogativa fica onde a resp: The question word goes where the answer would go: คุณชื่ออะไร = 'you are called what?'. Nothing is inverted. Analogy: it's leaving a blank space in the sentence — the other person just fills it in.
Acrescente ไหม (mǎi) no fim de uma afirm: Add ไหม (mǎi) at the end of a statement to turn it into a question. There is no universal 'yes' and 'no': you answer by repeating the verb (กิน = yes; ไม่กิน = no). Analogy: it is the 'right?' at the end of the sentence, except it actually turns it into a question.
Adjective + กว่า (gwàa) + term = 'more ... than'. Adjective + ที่สุด (tîi-sùt) = 'the most'. There is no word for 'more' before the adjective. Analogy: กว่า is the two-pan balance scale; ที่สุด is the podium.
Adjetivo como predicado, depois do subst: Adjective as predicate, after the noun
Direct adjective, without a linking verb.
Adjetivos funcionam como verbos de estad: Adjectives work as stative verbs: they don't use 'to be' (เป็น is a mistake here). And they come after the noun: บ้านใหม่ = new house. Analogy: the food 'tasty-is' — the adjective already has the verb built in.
Advérbios e intensificadores depois do v: Adverbs and intensifiers after the verb
Além de ครับ/ค่ะ, o fim da frase carrega: Besides ครับ/ค่ะ, the end of the sentence carries the emotion: นะ (ná) softens and asks for agreement ('okay?'), สิ (sì) encourages ('go on!'), หรอก (rɔ̀ɔk) softens a negation. Analogy: they are the emojis of Thai speech.
Antes do verbo, ได้ (dâai) indica que a: Before the verb, ได้ (dâai) indicates that the action actually occurred or there was an opportunity: ผมได้ไปเชียงใหม่. After the verb, ได้ is ability (A1). Analogy: before the verb it's the used ticket; after the verb it's the driver's license.
Causa e concessão: เพราะ, จึง, แม้ว่า: Cause and concession: เพราะ, จึง, แม้ว่า
Causative: X ให้ Y + verb.
Como determinante, นี้ (este), นั้น (ess: As a determiner, นี้ (this), นั้น (that) and โน้น (that over there) close the phrase, after the classifier: เสื้อ ตัว นี้ = this shirt. Alone, as a pronoun, use นี่/นั่น: นี่อะไร = what is this? Analogy: the classifier is the handle, the demonstrative is the pointing finger.
Como você se chama? (literalmente: você: What is your name? (literally: you are called what?)
Comparativo กว่า e superlativo ที่สุด: Comparative กว่า and superlative ที่สุด
Comparison between two: กว่า.
Demonstrativos: นี้, นั้น, โน้น e นี่, น: Demonstratives: นี้, นั้น, โน้น and นี่, นั่น
Depois de verbos de dizer, pensar e sabe: After verbs of saying, thinking and knowing (บอก, คิด, รู้), ว่า (wâa) introduces the content: ผมคิดว่า... = I think that... Analogy: ว่า opens the invisible quotation marks of what was said or thought.
Depois do verbo, ไป e มา dão direção (pa: After the verb, ไป and มา give direction (away from or towards the speaker) and ไว้ (wái) indicates keeping for later: เอามา = to bring, เอาไป = to take, จดไว้ = to note down (and keep). Analogy: arrows attached to the verb — over there, over here, or into the drawer.
He said THAT he will arrive late: บอกว่า.
Esta comida não é apimentada: ไม่ antes: This food is not spicy: ไม่ before the adjective. ไหม (rising tone) is the question particle.
Experiência com เคย; 'ainda não' com ยัง: Experience with เคย; 'not yet' with ยังไม่
Futuro e intenção com จะ: Future and intention with จะ
Homem fecha com ครับ, em qualquer situaç: Men close with ครับ, in any situation.
Older sister saying goodbye to the youngest.
Modo e intensidade vêm depois do verbo o: Manner and intensity come after the verb or adjective: พูดเร็ว (speaks fast), เดินช้า (walks slowly), อร่อยมาก (very tasty). Intensifiers: มาก (very), จัง (very, colloquial: ร้อนจัง), จริงๆ (really), ไป (too much: แพงไป). ค่อนข้าง (quite, somewhat) comes before: ค่อนข้างแพง. Analogy: Thai says first the what, then the how much.
Women, new and polite situation: ดิฉัน.
Na Tailândia chama-se pelo primeiro nome: In Thailand, people are called by their first name, never by their surname: คุณ + name (คุณสมชาย). Almost everyone has a short ชื่อเล่น (nickname) — ต้น, นก, เล็ก, ปุ้ย —, which is the everyday name, even at work. Teachers are อาจารย์ or ครู + name. Analogy: it's like Brazil, where the president can be called by a nickname — the surname hardly ever appears.
No fim da frase, quem FALA marca a polid: At the end of the sentence, the SPEAKER marks politeness: men use ครับ (kráp); women use ค่ะ (kâ) in statements and คะ (ká) in questions. Analogy: it is the signature at the end of an email — without it, the sentence sounds blunt or even rude.
The older person refers to themselves as พี่.
O possuidor vem depois da coisa: บ้าน (ข: The possessor comes after the thing: บ้าน (ของ) ผม = house (of) me → my house. ของ (kɔ̌ɔng) is optional when the relationship is obvious (family, body). Analogy: it's the 'of' in 'the house of Pedro', which sometimes drops in speech.
O sinal ๆ (mái yá-mók) repete a palavra: The symbol ๆ (mái yá-mók) repeats the previous word: เร็วๆ = really fast; เด็กๆ = the children (vague plural); ช้าๆ = slowly. Analogy: it's the 'encore' of a show — repeating adds emphasis or softens, depending on the context.
O tailandês encadeia verbos sem conectiv: Thai chains verbs without a connector, in the order of events: ไป ซื้อ ของ = go buy things; เดิน ไป ตลาด = walk to the market. Analogy: an assembly line — each verb does one stage of the same action.
O tailandês segue a ordem SVO, como o po: Thai follows SVO order, like Portuguese, but the verb never changes: there is no conjugation, gender, number, or tense in the word form. Analogy: words are LEGO pieces with a fixed shape — meaning comes from the order of assembly and from small extra words (jà, lɛ́ɛo), never from deforming the piece.
O verbo sozinho já é uma ordem (นั่ง = s: The verb alone is already a command (นั่ง = sit!). อย่า + verb = don't do it (อย่าลืม = don't forget); ห้าม + verb = it's forbidden, typical on signs (ห้ามสูบบุหรี่); ต้อง = have to; ไม่ต้อง = don't need to. นะ and หน่อย soften it: อย่าลืมนะ. Analogy: อย่า is a mother's advice; ห้าม is the inspector's sign.
O verbo tailandês nunca muda: ไป é 'vou': The Thai verb never changes: ไป is 'go', 'went' and 'will go'. Time comes from the surrounding words — เมื่อวาน (yesterday), วันนี้ (today), พรุ่งนี้ (tomorrow), ปีที่แล้ว (last year) — and from the markers จะ (future), กำลัง (in progress) and แล้ว (completed). Analogy: the verb is a photo without a date; the time words are the stamp that says when it was taken.
Orações de tempo: ก่อน, หลังจาก, ตอนที่,: Time clauses: ก่อน, หลังจาก, ตอนที่, จนกว่า
Ordem e proibição: อย่า, ห้าม, ต้อง, ไม่: Commands and prohibition: อย่า, ห้าม, ต้อง, ไม่ต้อง
Os termos de família viram pronomes, inc: Family terms become pronouns, even with strangers: พี่ (someone a bit older), น้อง (younger, also young waiters and staff), ลุง and ป้า (much older, parents' age), ตา and ยาย (elderly). The person uses the same term for themselves: พี่ไปก่อนนะ = 'I (the older one) am heading off'. Girls and young women sometimes say หนู to refer to themselves with older people. Analogy: it's the 'auntie' and 'uncle' Brazilian children use with any adult — except the whole system works this way.
Palavra interrogativa no lugar da respos: Question word in the place of the answer
Para contar: กาแฟ สอง แก้ว = 'café dois: To count: กาแฟ สอง แก้ว = 'coffee two cup'. Each type of thing has its classifier: คน (people), ตัว (animals, clothes), เล่ม (books), ใบ (sheets, tickets), อัน (objects in general). Analogy: in English we say 'two head of cattle' or 'three sheets of paper' — Thai does this always.
Para ordinais, coloca-se ที่ antes do nú: For ordinals, ที่ is placed before the number: ที่หนึ่ง (first), ที่สอง (second), ชั้นที่สาม (third floor), ครั้งที่ห้า (fifth time). 'First' can also be แรก, after the noun: วันแรก (the first day). Analogy: ที่ is the 'º' of 1º, 2º.
Para pedir uma coisa: ขอ + coisa (+ หน่อ: To ask for a thing: ขอ + thing (+ หน่อย): ขอน้ำหน่อย = can I have some water? To ask for an action: ช่วย + verb (+ หน่อย): ช่วยปิดประตูหน่อย = close the door, please. หน่อย ('a little bit') softens the request; ครับ/ค่ะ at the end completes the politeness. Analogy: หน่อย is the 'just a little please' — it reduces the weight of what is asked.
Partículas de polidez: ครับ, ค่ะ, คะ: Politeness particles: ครับ, ค่ะ, คะ
Partículas finais: นะ, สิ, หรอก: Final particles: นะ, สิ, หรอก
Pedindo: ขอ, ช่วย, หน่อย: Requesting: ขอ, ช่วย, หน่อย
Asking for something: ขอ + thing + หน่อย.
Pergunta de mulher: คะ (tom alto), não ค: A woman's question: คะ (high tone), not ค่ะ.
Perguntas de confirmação: ใช่ไหม, หรือเป: Confirmation questions: ใช่ไหม, หรือเปล่า, หรือยัง, เหรอ
Official prohibition sign: ห้าม.
Preço e quantidade: เท่าไร e กี่: Price and quantity: เท่าไร and กี่
Teacher + name: อาจารย์มาลี.
School teacher: คุณครู + name.
Pronomes pessoais e o sujeito que some: Personal pronouns and the subject that disappears
Quantificadores: ทุก, แต่ละ, บาง, หลาย,: Quantifiers: ทุก, แต่ละ, บาง, หลาย, ทั้ง
Saber, poder, aguentar: ได้, เป็น, ไหว: Knowing how, being able, enduring: ได้, เป็น, ไหว
Três 'conseguir' diferentes depois do ve: Three different 'can' after the verb: ได้ (it's possible, I have permission: ไปได้), เป็น (I know how because I learned: ว่ายน้ำเป็น = I can swim) and ไหว (I have the strength for it: เดินไม่ไหว = I can't walk anymore). Analogy: ได้ is the open door, เป็น is the diploma, ไหว is the battery.
Verbos de direção e resultado: มา, ไป, ไ: Verbs of direction and result: มา, ไป, ไว้
Vêm antes do classificador: ทุกคน (todos: They come before the classifier: ทุกคน (everyone), แต่ละคน (each one), บางคน (some people), หลายคน (several people), ทั้งวัน (the whole day). ทุก sees the group as a block; แต่ละ looks one by one. Analogy: ทุก is the class photo; แต่ละ is roll call, name by name.
กัน (gan) depois do verbo indica ação mú: กัน (gan) after the verb indicates mutual or joint action: รักกัน = they love each other; ไปกินข้าวกัน = let's go eat (together). Analogy: กัน is a handshake — it takes at least two.
กัน (juntos) pede sujeito plural: พวกเรา: กัน (together) requires a plural subject: พวกเรา.
กำลัง (em andamento) e แล้ว (já, concluí: กำลัง (in progress) and แล้ว (already, completed)
กำลัง (gam-lang) antes do verbo = estar: กำลัง (gam-lang) before the verb = doing right now. แล้ว (lɛ́ɛo) at the end = already happened or a change of state. Analogy: กำลัง is the ▶ button (in progress) and แล้ว is the ✔ (completed).
ก่อน(ที่) = antes de; หลังจาก = depois d: ก่อน(ที่) = before; หลังจาก = after; ตอนที่ = when; จนกว่า = until. The time clause can come before or after the main clause. Analogy: markers on a timeline — you plant the flag and say what came before or after.
คุณ + first name: the polite standard.
จะ (jà) antes do verbo marca futuro ou i: จะ (jà) before the verb marks future or intention. Often a time word (พรุ่งนี้) is enough. Analogy: it's the 'going to' in 'going to eat' — an intention label stuck before the verb.
ดื่ม (to drink) + กาแฟ (coffee).
ถูก (tùuk) + agente + verbo forma uma pa: ถูก (tùuk) + agent + verb forms a passive used mainly for bad things: ผมถูกหมากัด = I was bitten by a dog. For neutral or good facts, the active voice is preferred. Analogy: ถูก is a 'caution' sign — it warns that the subject suffered something.
ถ้า (tâa) abre a condição; ก็ (gɔ̂ɔ) cos: ถ้า (tâa) opens the condition; ก็ (gɔ̂ɔ) usually marks the consequence, before the verb of the second clause. Analogy: ถ้า is the 'if' of the traffic light and ก็ is the 'then go' that lights up afterwards.
ที่ (tîi) liga um substantivo à oração q: ที่ (tîi) links a noun to the clause that describes it: คนที่ใส่หมวก = the person who wears a hat. It comes right after the noun. Analogy: ที่ is the hook where the description is hung.
ผม (eu, homem), ดิฉัน (eu, mulher, forma: ผม (I, male), ดิฉัน (I, female, formal), ฉัน (I, female, informal), เรา (we; also informal 'I'), คุณ (you), เขา (he or she), พวกเขา/พวกเรา (they, we). มัน is 'it' and works for animals; used for people, it offends. When the context makes it clear, the subject simply disappears: ไปไหน? = 'where are (you) going?'. Analogy: like in English 'Going to the store' — no one needs to say 'I'.
พูด (falar) é o verbo que combina com ภา: พูด (to speak) is the verb that goes with ภาษาไทย (Thai language).
ยัง + verbo + อยู่ = ainda estar fazendo: ยัง + verb + อยู่ = still doing: เขายังนอนอยู่. เพิ่ง (pə̂ng) + verb = just did: ผมเพิ่งมา. Analogy: ยัง...อยู่ is the light still on; เพิ่ง is the paint still fresh.
ยัง ... อยู่ (ainda) e เพิ่ง (acabar de): ยัง ... อยู่ (still) and เพิ่ง (just)
ว่า: dizer, pensar, saber que: ว่า: to say, think, know that
อยาก (yàak) + verbo = querer fazer; ต้อง: อยาก (yàak) + verb = want to do; ต้อง (dtɔ̂ng) + verb = need to; ได้ (dâai) AFTER the verb = can, know how to do. Analogy: อยาก is the heart (desire), ต้อง is the clock (obligation) and ได้ is the tool (ability) — and the tool goes at the end of the sentence.
เคย (kəəi) + verbo = já ter feito alguma: เคย (kəəi) + verb = have done at some point. For 'not yet', use ยังไม่ + verb. Analogy: เคย is the stamp in the passport — proof you've been there; ยังไม่ is the page still blank.
เท่าไร (tâo-rài) pergunta 'quanto' (preç: เท่าไร (tâo-rài) asks 'how much' (price, value) and goes at the end. กี่ (gìi) asks 'how many' and requires a classifier: กี่คน = how many people. Analogy: เท่าไร is the price tag; กี่ is counting on your fingers — and each finger asks for a classifier.
เป็น (bpen) liga o sujeito a uma categor: เป็น (bpen) links the subject to a category or profession; คือ (kʉʉ) equates and defines (X is exactly Y); อยู่ (yùu) gives location. Analogy: เป็น is the drawer label, คือ is the equals sign (=) and อยู่ is the address.
เป็น, คือ e อยู่: três 'ser/estar': เป็น, คือ and อยู่: three 'to be'
เพราะ(ว่า) dá a causa; จึง (jʉng) marca: เพราะ(ว่า) gives the cause; จึง (jʉng) marks the result; แม้ว่า (mɛ́ɛ-wâa) = although, with ก็ in the second clause. Analogy: เพราะ is the root, จึง is the fruit; แม้ว่า is rowing against the current and still arriving.
ใช่ไหม confirma uma suposição (não é?);: ใช่ไหม confirms an assumption (isn't it?); หรือเปล่า asks whether something happened or is true (or not?); หรือยัง asks whether it has happened yet (already… or not yet?); เหรอ (spoken; written หรือ) shows surprise (really?). หรือยัง is answered with …แล้ว (already) or ยัง (not yet). Analogy: they are four shades of question mark.
ให้ (hâi) tem três usos: dar (ให้ของขวัญ: ให้ (hâi) has three uses: to give (ให้ของขวัญ); to make or let someone do something (หมอให้ผมพัก); and 'for someone' after the verb (ซื้อให้แม่). Analogy: ให้ is a delivery arrow — for an object, an order, or a favor.
ให้: dar, mandar fazer, para alguém: ให้: to give, to have someone do, for someone
ได้ antes do verbo: aconteceu, teve a ch: ได้ before the verb: it happened, had the chance
ไม่ (mâi) vai imediatamente antes do ver: ไม่ (mâi) goes immediately before the verb or adjective being negated. Analogy: it is a switch placed right before the lamp — it turns off only the next word.
